candidates.title: fix: quantity double-counted in GraphQL gross_sales / line_item_enhanced (fixes #165)
fix_lines: | [`shopify_gql__orders`](https://fivetran.github.io/dbt_shopify/#!/model/model.shopify.shopify_gql__orders), [`shopify_gql__daily_shop`](https://fivetran.github.io/dbt_shopify/#!/model/model.shopify.shopify_gql__daily_shop) | Column value | `gross_sales` / `net_sales` = `Σ quantity² × unit_price` | `gross_sales` / `net_sales` = `Σ quantity × unit_price` | Fixes a bug where GraphQL orders with any line `quantity > 1` had sales figures inflated quadratically. Orders where every line has `quantity = 1` are unaffected. |

fix_lines:
| `zendesk__ticket_field_history`
`zendesk__ticket_backlog`
`int_zendesk__field_history_pivot`
(Breaking) | Changed column | `status_status` | `status` | Fixes column naming conflicts when a custom field shares a title with a standard field. Also removes unintended `_` columns. Only affects configurations with these conflicts. |

- Fixes `zendesk__ticket_backlog` failing when a custom ticket field shares a title with a standard field (for example, `Status`). Standard fields now retain their names; custom fields can be tracked separately by adding their numeric IDs to `ticket_field_history_columns` (for example, `status_<field_id>`).

- Fixes failures when custom ticket field titles contain no Latin letters or numbers (for example, `購入段階`). These fields can be tracked regardless of title using their numeric IDs, with a leading underscore (for example, `_<field_id>`).

candidates.title: Fix: Ignore reopened solves in reply time SLAs and apply internal_user_criteria to audit-log roles (v1.9.1)
fix_lines: - Fixes `internal_user_criteria` not applying to comments from users whose historical support role was `not set` or `end-user`. Affects `zendesk__ticket_metrics` and `zendesk__sla_policies`.
- Fixes inflated `first_reply_time` and `next_reply_time` values and missed SLA breaches in `zendesk__sla_policies` for tickets that were solved and then reopened before the reply.

candidates.title: Fix false first_reply_time SLA breaches to match Zendesk's own determination (v1.9.0)
fix_lines: - Fixes false `first_reply_time` SLA breaches in `zendesk__sla_policies`. `sla_applied_at` for `first_reply_time` now uses the application time Zendesk logs in `ticket_field_history`. The SLA clock now starts when Zendesk starts it; for a ticket created on a customer's behalf with a private comment, that's the customer's first comment.

- Fixes a related false breach when Zendesk re-applies the `first_reply_time` target to a ticket that was already replied to, such as after a priority change. `sla_applied_at` now always anchors to the earliest logged application for the ticket instead of the latest, so an already-satisfied reply is no longer discarded.
- As above, `sla_event_id` also changes for the `first_reply_time` events affected by this fix.

candidates.title: Fix SLA breach on tickets with no real external customer (v1.9.0-a2)
fix_lines: - Fixes false `first_reply_time` SLA breaches for tickets with no real external requester (e.g. an agent filing a ticket on their own behalf). The a1 fix below disqualified an agent's early reply until "the customer" engaged, but on these tickets no customer ever will, so the reply now counts normally against the ticket's creation time, matching Zendesk's behavior.

candidates.title: Fix false first-reply SLA breaches on privately-created tickets (RD-1277353)
fix_lines: - Fixes false `first_reply_time` SLA breaches in `zendesk__sla_policies` for tickets created on a customer's behalf via private/internal comments. For these tickets, the SLA clock now starts at the customer's first comment, public or private, matching Zendesk's behavior. An agent's own comment no longer counts as a reply until the customer has engaged, which can also surface previously-hidden breaches where a proactive agent comment was wrongly counted as the reply. `zendesk__ticket_metrics` is unchanged and may differ due to its intentionally separate `first_reply_time` definition (see `DECISIONLOG.md`).

candidates.title: Resolve custom ticket field IDs to readable names (RD-1260302)
fix_lines: - Resolves custom ticket field IDs in the `ticket_field_history_columns` variable to their actual field titles, so `int_zendesk__field_history_pivot` and `zendesk__ticket_backlog` use readable custom field names instead of raw numeric IDs. Custom fields can be referenced by either their numeric ID or their `title`. If multiple custom fields resolve to the same title, the raw field ID is appended to keep column names unique, and a field with no title falls back to its ID. Standard fields (`status`, `priority`, etc.) are unaffected.
